title: The Quiet Semester
premise: Coral Crane has spent senior year as the invisible statistician of her school's championship swim team, quietly tracking the impossible times that prove someone is doping the athletes. When her best friend Priya vanishes days before prom, leaving only a ring of keys to the aquatic center, Coral must decide whether to keep counting or start speaking. Following the keys through locked offices and buried records, she uncovers a doping scheme run by the beloved head coach and protected by families who profit from scholarships. In the end, Coral testifies at the district hearing, costing her the friendship of the team captain who knew and stayed silent—but winning back Priya, who returns having gathered her own evidence, and earning a graduation she finally believes she deserves.
about_author: L. M. Ashgrove is the pen name of a former high school math tutor who spent three seasons timing swimmers from a folding chair at the pool's edge. They write quiet thrillers about teenagers who notice what adults hope they won't.

chapters.title: Split Times
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. During a dual meet, Coral logs relay splits that are physiologically impossible and says nothing, as always. She counts down 94 days to graduation in her notebook. Emotional beat: the comfort and suffocation of being the one who sees everything and reports nothing.

chapters.title: The Statistician's Vow
chapters.summary: Flashback woven into present: freshman-year Coral, after an older teammate's career ended mysteriously, promised herself invisibility keeps people safe. Priya teases her for it over fries. Emotional beat: establishing the friendship as Coral's one exception to silence.

chapters.title: Ninety-Four Days
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coach Deacon announces scholarship scouts will attend the state qualifier, and the team celebrates while Coral's spreadsheet of anomalous times grows a new column. Priya seems distracted, asking odd questions about the equipment room. Emotional beat: dread disguised as routine.

chapters.title: Keys
chapters.summary: Priya misses their morning coffee ritual. By evening, her mother calls Coral in panic—Priya never came home. At Priya's locker, Coral finds only a labeled keyring: pool office, storage cage, and a key with no tag. Emotional beat: guilt arriving before grief.

chapters.title: What Missing Looks Like
chapters.summary: Alternating Coral and Priya's mother's accounts. Police call it a runaway; the school closes ranks; teammates post worried messages they clearly rehearsed. Coral notices Captain Dana Whitlock watching her, not the door. Emotional beat: the first crack in the team's polished surface.

chapters.title: The Storage Cage
chapters.summary: Coral uses the untagged key at night and finds boxes of supplement shipments addressed to a name that isn't Coach Deacon's—and a second ledger matching her own numbers. Someone was already counting. Emotional beat: terror and vindication holding hands.

chapters.title: Dana Whitlock Knows Something
chapters.summary: Coral confronts Dana gently; Dana deflects with loyalty talk about the team's future and warns Coral not to 'make things worse for everyone.' Coral recognizes the language of complicity. Emotional beat: love against duty, first collision.

chapters.title: The Ledger's Second Hand
chapters.summary: Coral cross-references the found ledger and realizes the handwriting belongs to Priya—she'd been investigating for months. A torn page lists a date: the night Priya disappeared. Emotional beat: betrayal by no one, and the horror of a friend who carried this alone.

chapters.title: Coach Deacon's Office
chapters.summary: Using the office key, Coral photographs files linking Deacon to a booster club funneling scholarship money contingent on results. Deacon nearly catches her; his kindness afterward is more frightening than anger would be. Emotional beat: the price of survival made flesh.

chapters.title: A Text from Priya
chapters.summary: A message arrives from Priya's number: 'Stop looking.' Coral can't tell if it's coercion or protection. She replies with a statistic only Priya would understand—a coded signal from their freshman codebook. Emotional beat: hope weaponized into risk.

chapters.title: The Booster Dinner
chapters.summary: Coral attends the boosters' fundraiser as the invisible stat girl, cataloguing who sits where. She overhears a parent and Deacon discussing 'the Priya situation' as a solved problem. Emotional beat: rage crystallizing into purpose.

chapters.title: Confession at the Pool
chapters.summary: Coral tells Dana everything she's found. Dana admits she suspected but signed a silent scholarship agreement her family depends on. She begs Coral to wait until after state. Emotional beat: the friendship-before-prom fracture beginning.

chapters.title: Prom Dress, Empty Chair
chapters.summary: A quieter chapter: Coral and her mother alter a prom dress bought for two best friends. Coral reads Priya's old texts and finds a half-deleted draft: 'If I go missing, it wasn't my choice.' Emotional beat: grief sharpened into resolve.

chapters.title: The Untagged Key
chapters.summary: Coral finally tries the third key: it opens a maintenance tunnel beneath the bleachers where Priya stashed a waterproof bag—her full evidence file and a note naming her source inside the athletic department. Emotional beat: Priya planned to be found.

chapters.title: State Qualifier
chapters.summary: Meet day. Coral watches swimmers she loves drop times that could kill them, and Deacon beams beside her. Dana swims clean for the first time in a year and loses badly, then looks at Coral across the deck. Emotional beat: the cost of integrity made visible.

chapters.title: Where Priya Went
chapters.summary: Following the note's lead, Coral tracks Priya's source—the assistant athletic director—to a motel outside town and finds Priya hiding there, scared but unharmed, having fled when Deacon threatened her family's visa status. Emotional beat: reunion that feels like surfacing for air.

chapters.title: Two Ledgers, One Truth
chapters.summary: Coral and Priya reconcile their data into an undeniable case. Priya wants to go public immediately; Coral hesitates, knowing testimony will end the team, Dana's scholarship, and her own anonymity forever. Emotional beat: the decision the whole book has been counting toward.

chapters.title: The Night Before Prom
chapters.summary: Deacon corners Coral with a veiled offer: a paid stats internship, her mother's debts mentioned too precisely. Coral declines. That night, Dana learns Coral testified-bound and ends their friendship in the parking lot. Emotional beat: every price comes due at once.

chapters.title: Prom
chapters.summary: Coral goes anyway, wearing the altered dress, and publicly hands Principal Reyes the evidence envelope before the first dance. The gym goes silent; Deacon is escorted out mid-song. Emotional beat: climax—truth spoken in the room where everyone can see.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: District hearing. Coral presents both ledgers; Priya testifies; Dana, after a long silence, corroborates the scholarship agreements, sacrificing her own eligibility. Deacon and the booster president are barred from athletics. Emotional beat: duty fulfilled, love redefined.

chapters.title: Graduation Day
chapters.summary: Coral walks the stage having stopped counting days. Dana approaches afterward—not forgiveness yet, but honesty, and maybe a start. Priya stands beside her in the crowd. Emotional beat: inheritance refused; a future chosen rather than served.

chapters.title: Epilogue: The New Statistician
chapters.summary: Fall semester. Coral, now a college freshman, mentors a nervous younger student who noticed something wrong on her own team and doesn't know what to do. Coral hands her a notebook and says, 'Start counting.' Emotional beat: the cycle broken, passed forward as courage instead of silence.
